canonical_task: CYK recognition, O(n^3)
citation: Jones & Laaser, Complete problems for deterministic polynomial time, TCS 3 (1976)

canonical_task: computable in P by iterated low-degree deletion
citation: Anderson & Mayr, A P-complete problem and approximations to it (1984)

canonical_task: bottom-up fixpoint evaluation, poly-time in the data
citation: Dantsin, Eiter, Gottlob & Voronkov, Complexity and expressive power of logic programming, ACM Comput. Surv. 33 (2001)

canonical_task: run GE with partial pivoting, poly-time
citation: Vavasis, Gaussian elimination with pivoting is P-complete, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2 (1989)

canonical_task: breadth-depth search ordering is P-complete
citation: Greenlaw (1993); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: CFG emptiness/productivity is P-complete
citation: Jones & Laaser (1976); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: Metric Dimension decision: resolving set of size <= k?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: GJ [GT61]; Khuller-Raghavachari-Rosenfeld 1996 (Khuller, Raghavachari & Rosenfeld, Landmarks in graphs, Discrete Appl. Math. 70 (1996) 217-229)

canonical_task: Acyclic k-Colorability decision: a(G) <= k? (NP-complete already for k=3)
citation: Kostochka, Upper bounds of chromatic functions of graphs (1978); acyclic 3-colouring NP-complete for planar bipartite max-degree-4 graphs: Ochem, Negative results on acyclic improper colorings, EuroComb 2005
note: NP-complete for every fixed k>=3 (Kostochka 1978; Coleman-Cai); Ochem (2005) sharpens to planar bipartite Delta<=4. Distinct from proper colouring / star colouring (S2)

canonical_task: Biclique Cover decision: cover all edges with <= k bicliques?
citation: Orlin, Contentment in graph theory: covering graphs with cliques, Indag. Math. 39 (1977) 406-424
note: NP-complete (Orlin 1977). Distinct from biclique PARTITION and from Maximum Edge Biclique (S2)

canonical_task: Closest Substring decision: a length-L center within distance d of some substring of each input?
citation: Lanctot, Li, Ma, Wang & Zhang, Distinguishing string selection problems, Inform. Comput. 185 (2003) 41-55; Li, Ma & Wang, J. ACM 49 (2002)
note: NP-complete; generalizes Closest String (L = full length). Distinct from Closest String (S2)

canonical_task: 3-Path Vertex Cover decision: a set of <= k vertices meeting every P3 (equivalently dissociation number >= n-k)?
citation: Orlovich, Dolgui, Finke, Gordon & Werner, The complexity of dissociation set problems in graphs, Discrete Appl. Math. 159 (2011) 1352-1366; Yannakakis (1981, node-deletion)
note: NP-hard to compute the dissociation number / minimum 3-path vertex cover. Distinct from Vertex Cover (P2 cover) and Independent Set (S2)

canonical_task: F3||Cmax decision: makespan <= t? strongly NP-complete for 3 machines
citation: Garey, Johnson & Sethi, The complexity of flowshop and jobshop scheduling, Mathematics of Operations Research 1 (1976) 117-129
note: F2||Cmax is in P (Johnson's rule); F3||Cmax is strongly NP-complete -> a decoupling threshold

canonical_task: Graph Genus decision: does G embed in the genus-g orientable surface? NP-complete
citation: Thomassen, The graph genus problem is NP-complete, Journal of Algorithms 10 (1989) 568-576

canonical_task: JISP decision: schedule >= k jobs (<=1 disjoint interval each)? NP-complete
citation: Spieksma, On the approximability of an interval scheduling problem, Journal of Scheduling 2 (1999) 215-227
note: introduced by Nakajima & Hakimi 1982; NP-completeness/APX-hardness by Spieksma 1999

canonical_task: MAX-E3-SAT decision: satisfy >= k of the exact-3 clauses? NP-complete (contains 3-SAT)
citation: Hastad, Some optimal inapproximability results, Journal of the ACM 48 (2001) 798-859
note: decision NP-complete via 3-SAT (Cook-Levin); the tight approximation story is Hastad 2001

canonical_task: MRCT decision: spanning tree of routing cost <= B?
citation: Johnson, Lenstra & Rinnooy Kan, The complexity of the network design problem, Networks 8 (1978) 279-285
note: OCT NP-hard (JLRK 1978); the uniform-requirement routing-cost version (MRCT) is also NP-hard

canonical_task: Optimal Decision Tree decision: an identification tree of cost <= B?
citation: Hyafil & Rivest, Constructing optimal binary decision trees is NP-complete, Inform. Process. Lett. 5 (1976) 15-17

canonical_task: Test Cover decision: a distinguishing subfamily of <= k tests?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Minimum Test Set, SP6]

canonical_task: Orienteering decision: a walk of length <= B collecting reward >= R?
citation: Blum, Chawla, Karger, Lane, Meyerson & Minkoff, Approximation algorithms for orienteering and discounted-reward TSP, SIAM J. Comput. 37 (2007) 653-670

canonical_task: P|prec|Cmax decision: a precedence-respecting schedule of makespan <= T?
citation: Ullman, NP-complete scheduling problems, JCSS 10 (1975) 384-393
note: NP-complete (Ullman 1975); NP-hard even with unit processing times

canonical_task: Red-Blue Set Cover decision: cover all blue while covering <= k red?
citation: Carr, Doddi, Konjevod & Marathe, On the red-blue set cover problem, SODA 2000, 345-353

canonical_task: Unsigned reversal distance decision: sortable in <= k reversals?
citation: Caprara, Sorting permutations by reversals and Eulerian cycle decompositions, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 12 (1999) 91-110
note: UNSIGNED sorting by reversals is NP-hard (Caprara 1997/1999); the SIGNED version is in P (Hannenhalli & Pevzner 1995) — a separate object (S2)

canonical_task: Subset Product: a subset with product = P?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [SP14]
note: NP-complete (reduction from Exact Cover by 3-Sets); remains NP-hard with polynomially-bounded elements

canonical_task: R||Cmax decision: an assignment with makespan <= T?
citation: Lenstra, Shmoys & Tardos, Approximation algorithms for scheduling unrelated parallel machines, Math. Programming 46 (1990) 259-271

canonical_task: maximum antichain (poset width) >= k: in P via Dilworth's theorem realized as a bipartite matching / minimum chain cover — finding and optimizing antichains is poly, the decoupling witness against #P-complete counting
citation: Fulkerson, Note on Dilworth's decomposition theorem for partially ordered sets, Proc. AMS 7 (1956) 701-702
note: poly-time maximum antichain via bipartite matching (Fulkerson 1956), from Dilworth, Ann. of Math. 51 (1950) 161-166

canonical_task: spanning-tree existence = connectivity of G; decided in linear time by DFS/BFS
citation: Tarjan, Depth-first search and linear graph algorithms, SIAM J. Comput. 1(2) (1972) 146-160
note: connectivity (hence spanning-tree existence) in linear time
